chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Saeed al-Sabiri (the seller of Sabir), who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Can the man weep during the prayer?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Congratulations! Congratulations, and even though it (tears) may be the like of the head of a fly'.

key_terms.بَخْ: an expression of approval or congratulations
key_terms.رَأْسُ الذُّبَاب: the head of a fly (used to denote a very small amount)
key_terms.يَتَبَاكَى: to weep profusely or show signs of weeping

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to weep during Islamic prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the practice of weeping during prayer, using the phrase 'Bakh bakh' to denote high approval even for minimal tears. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *khushu'* (humility) and emotional connection with the Divine, where the sincerity of the heart outweighs the physical quantity of tears. The narration underscores that such emotional expression is a sign of deep spiritual presence (*hudur al-qalb*) rather than a distraction.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Saeed Baya’a Al Sabiry who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Can the man weep during the Salāt?’ So heasws said: ‘Congratulations! Congratulations, and even though it (tears) may be the like of the head of a fly’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from Sa‘id al- Bayya’ al-Sabiriy who has said the following:

“I asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Can a person weep during Salah (prayer)?’ The Imam replied, ‘It is a matter of great congratulations even if it (tears) is of the size of the head of a fly.’”
